A concise, non-operational overview of protective factors:
Standoff distance
: the greater the distance between vehicles and the structure, the lower the blast load on critical elements.
Access control
: restricted curb access, screened loading docks, and controlled garages reduce exposure.
Perimeter hardening
: bollards, planters, barriers, and street design can prevent close vehicle approach.
Structural robustness
: redundancy and progressive-collapse resistance improve resilience.
Façade design
: laminated glazing and anchored curtain walls reduce hazardous debris.
Critical-element protection
: shielding columns, transfer structures, utility rooms, and lobbies lowers consequences.
Emergency preparedness
: evacuation planning, surveillance, and coordination with police/fire reduce harm.
